trust_decision.summary: Whether the hostname resolves to an internal address is decided only by a regex over the string returned by options.resolveDNSHost (throwOnLoopback), and the verified address is then discarded: both fetches connect to the original hostname, which is resolved again, so the check and the connection are not bound together.

landing_point.why: The advisory is a DNS-rebinding bypass of the loopback check, so a reader goes to the resolveDNSHost -> throwOnLoopback pair that runs immediately before the fetch.

fix_sites.module_kind: library public API - initial outbound fetch
library public API - redirect-hop outbound fetch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The README presents resolveDNSHost as an optional mitigation ('you can use') and lists followRedirects 'follow' as supported while warning it is dangerous, so a solver can argue that any route which does not call the resolver, or that the caller told fetch to follow, is outside the library's documented guarantee.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: followRedirects:'manual' with a handleRedirects allowlist must keep following a legitimate HTTP->HTTPS or bare-domain->www redirect and return the redirected page; a fix that refuses redirects, or that validates the forwarded URL before the user's callback gets to accept it, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: bare dotted-quad IPv4 returned by resolveDNSHost (e.g. 93.184.216.34)
6to4 2002::/16 embedded IPv4 (handled by the fix's hextet check, fix.diff:218-220)
whole URLs returned from resolveDNSHost (http://127.0.0.1/, http://[::1]/)
a resolved value that is not an IP address at all, now rejected with 'must resolve to an IP address or URL' (fix.diff:763-765)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: followRedirects:'follow' - the redirect guard only runs when redirect === 'manual', so fetch follows the Location chain itself and every redirect target is fetched without validation or pinning; the published fix keeps the same manual-only gate (fix.diff:812).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The README documents 'follow' as a supported but dangerous opt-in, and the library cannot inspect fetch's internal redirect chain, so the caller who asked for it owns the risk.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~28 lines below the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: proxyUrl option - the request goes to proxyUrl + detectedUrl, so the address that resolveDNSHost validated is never the address connected to; the published fix still exempts the proxy path (fix.diff:787).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The proxy makes the outbound connection, so pinning the connection to the resolved IP is impossible without breaking TLS/Host, and the proxy is operator-configured infrastructure.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, at the landing point's fetch

O8_uncovered_routes.route: no resolveDNSHost callback - the else branch only console.errors a warning and the hostname is fetched unvalidated and unpinned.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The README presents resolveDNSHost as an optional option and this branch warns on stderr, so without a resolver there is nothing to compare and the caller opted out.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 3 lines below the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second address-block table (REGEX_LOOPBACK already lives here) consumed by a new isAllowedHost helper instead of the inline checks in index.ts.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already keeps its loopback knowledge in the constants module and a maintainer extending the block list would naturally edit that table rather than the guard, leaving the normalised/embedded-IPv4 forms uncovered in the new consumer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A proxy/composition URL builder: a second outbound-URL construction path (proxyUrl.concat(detectedUrl)) that does not use the validated address.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Proxy support already exists as an option-merge branch next to the fetch; a maintainer adding a configurable proxy helper would write another URL builder and forget to thread the pinned address through it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A multi-hop redirect loop: another fetch performed after following a second Location header, which must re-validate and re-pin the new host.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The manual redirect path already performs a second fetch; a maintainer extending it to follow several hops would add fetches that a fix aimed at the first two sites would not cover.
